llm.summary: This security suite is mostly purpose-aligned, but some auxiliary workflows can trust mutable or unsigned remote data that could steer security decisions or installs.

dimensions.detail: Reading installed skill names/versions, writing a local state file, and fetching advisory data are proportionate for this security purpose. I did not find artifact-backed credential collection or exfiltration; scanner hits in feed.json are vulnerability descriptions.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The recommended and guarded install paths use npx clawhub@latest, so installer behavior can change after review. The manual install path includes checksum/signature verification, which is safer.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The main hook verifies signed feeds, but HEARTBEAT.md fetches the advisory feed with curl, validates only JSON shape, and prints remote title/action text as operational security guidance. The catalog discovery script also accepts a remote catalog URL without signature or hostname restrictions and prints install commands from that data.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Setup can install a persistent global OpenClaw hook and optionally create an unattended main-session cron job. This is disclosed and preflighted, and the hook only posts alerts, but it is still high-impact agent automation that users should review before enabling.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose matches the artifacts: advisory monitoring, installed-skill matching, guarded installs, hook setup, optional cron setup, and local advisory state tracking are all disclosed and security-related.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review before installing. Prefer the manual verified install path or a pinned clawhub version, keep CLAWSEC_ALLOW_UNSIGNED_FEED disabled, avoid custom feed/catalog URLs unless you control and verify them, and only enable the persistent hook or cron if you want ongoing security automation in your OpenClaw main session.
llm.findings:
[YR1] expected: Downgraded: the matched process.env/fetch/Telegram text appears inside signed advisory-feed vulnerability descriptions, not executable credential-exfiltration code.
[TP4] expected: Partly accepted as review-relevant but not malicious: hook, cron, state, installed-skill scanning, and approval gating are disclosed in SKILL.md, skill.json, and HOOK.md.
[AE1] expected: Overridden: the referenced artifacts were locally present and inspected, including feed.json, guarded_skill_install.mjs, and discover_skill_catalog.mjs.
[YR4] expected: Downgraded: repeated description fields and security terms are expected in a large advisory feed and do not independently show tool poisoning or hidden instructions.
[PE3] expected: Downgraded: .env and credential terms are in advisory descriptions about vulnerabilities, not code that reads credential files.
[P1] expected: Downgraded: bypass-security language is advisory content describing vulnerabilities, not instructions to this evaluator or to a runtime agent.
[T01] unexpected: Accepted: HEARTBEAT.md fetches remote advisory JSON without signature verification and prints remote action/title fields into a periodic agent-facing workflow.
[T08] unexpected: Accepted: guarded_skill_install.mjs and documentation use mutable npx clawhub@latest for installs.
[T08] unexpected: Accepted: discover_skill_catalog.mjs fetches a remote catalog without signature verification or URL allowlisting and emits install commands using remote skill IDs.
